violations.why: Task writes v_cedar then ISR overwrites it before the task later reads v_cedar for v_harbor, creating a write‑write‑read race.
Task writes v_cedar, ISR can preempt and write a new value before the task later reads v_cedar in the fn_walnut condition, forming a write‑write‑read violation.
Task’s initial write to v_cedar may be overwritten by the ISR before the task reads v_cedar as an argument to fn_willow, yielding a write‑write‑read race.
The task reads v_cedar in the if‑condition, ISR can modify it, then the task reads v_cedar again for the fn_willow call, a read‑write‑read atomicity breach.
After the task reads v_cedar in fn_walnut, the ISR may change it before the later read for v_harbor, producing a read‑write‑read violation.
The task reads v_cedar as a fn_willow argument; ISR could write a new value before the subsequent read for v_harbor, creating a read‑write‑read race.
